correctness.rationale: Normalized monomial moments were derived from the actual radial cutoff; beta<2 is the sharp Dirichlet convergence boundary. Analytic continuation of the classical modified-Bessel integral yields the exact real spectrum, and the fixed-ray K asymptotic gives an absolute-envelope error O_beta(s^-1/2). Counting integers near phase zeros in x=sqrt(2s) produces only O_beta(L) exceptions, allowing the sharp beta-dependent L log L coefficient separately for both signs. The beta=3/2 elementary formula is exact. Direct numerical oscillatory quadrature, K values, and finite counts passed 93 supplementary tests. Infinity claims rest on the written proof, not numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: The unweighted Bergman disk and reciprocal-distance boundary oscillation are standard motivated objects. The leading squared-log spectral count is universal across a full beta interval, whereas its second L log L term detects the power of an increasingly singular boundary symbol; both positive and negative eigenvalues contribute equal leading and subleading counts. The same natural family exhibits all-Schatten cancellation and failure of the naive kernel diagonal trace formula, despite a non-L1 symbol, and includes an exact injective elementary Bessel case. This is a quantitative spectral classification, not merely a generic boundedness example or a low-effort substitution.
